findings.claim: The efficiency definition, the efficiency equation and the whole worked example sit inside <div class="higher-only">, which is display:none for Foundation readers.
findings.truth: P2.1.8 (recall and apply the efficiency equation) is not bold in the -bold file, and efficiency is not bold in the 5h equations list, so it is a recall equation at both tiers. The heading 'Efficiency and Dissipation' and the dissipation paragraph sat outside the wrapper, so a Foundation reader met the heading and then nothing about efficiency, while a knowledge check, a flashcard, a takeaway and a 4-mark practice question all test it untagged. Fixed by dropping the class from the wrapper div; div open and close counts unchanged.
findings.evidence: spec P2.1.8 and 5h (a) 'Recall and apply' table, neither bold

findings.claim: Q5 'Explain why electricity from power stations is transmitted at high voltage' is typed '3 marks - Explain (HT)'.
findings.truth: P3.4.6 and P2.2.5 are both unbold, so high-voltage transmission is assessed at both tiers. The (HT) tag is removed.

findings.claim: Q3 (electric fields) and Q5 (why static builds on insulators) are typed '3 marks - Explain (HT)'.
findings.truth: P3.1 is separate science only but contains no bold statements, so all three of its outcomes are assessed at both tiers. Both (HT) tags removed.

findings.claim: Q4 ('current gets smaller after a resistor' misconception) and Q6 (thermistor vs fixed resistor) are typed '3 marks - Explain (HT)'.
findings.truth: P3.2.1, P3.2.5 and P3.3.5c are unbold, so both are assessed at both tiers. Both (HT) tags removed.

findings.claim: Q5 is typed '4 marks - Required Practical Method'.
findings.truth: 'Required practical' is AQA and Edexcel wording. This board splits practical work into eight Practical Activity Groups, PAG1 to PAG8; investigating I-V characteristics is PAG6 (P3.2.6b). Retyped to 'Practical Method', the label already used across this subject.
findings.evidence: spec chapter P8 'OCR has split the requirements ... into eight Practical Activity Groups or PAGs'; P3.2.6b PAG6

findings.claim: 'The most heavily examined mistake in circuits is ...'
findings.truth: An invented exam claim. Nothing in the spec ranks how often a misconception appears. Reworded to 'the most common mistake'.
findings.evidence: house rule on invented exam claims

findings.claim: 'It operates at approximately 230 V and changes direction 50 times per second - a frequency of 50 Hz.'
findings.truth: 50 Hz means 50 complete cycles every second, and the current reverses twice in each cycle, so it changes direction 100 times a second. As written the lesson teaches a wrong number as fact for a statement learners must recall.
findings.evidence: settled fact: frequency = cycles per second; spec P2.2.4 'recall that the domestic supply in the UK is a.c., at 50 Hz and about 230 volts'

findings.claim: The whole 'Transformers and the National Grid' section (heading plus three paragraphs, including Vp Ip = Vs Is) is wrapped in <div class="higher-only">.
findings.truth: P2.2.5, P3.4.5 and P3.4.6 are all unbold, so transformers in the National Grid, the conservation-of-energy argument and high-voltage transmission are assessed at both tiers. Vp Ip = Vs Is is keyed to P3.4.5 in the equations list and is not bold there either. Foundation readers lost the section entirely while the third takeaway and a flashcard test the same idea untagged. Fixed by dropping the class; div counts unchanged.
findings.evidence: spec P2.2.5, P3.4.5, P3.4.6; 5h (b) row P3.4.5/P3.7.8a not bold

findings.claim: Q5 (why the National Grid uses high voltage, using P = I squared R) is typed '3 marks - Explain (HT)'.
findings.truth: P3.4.4b and P3.4.6 are unbold, so this is assessed at both tiers. Tag removed.

The LaTeX thousands separator sits outside the \( \) delimiters, so KaTeX never processes it and the student sees the braces. The arithmetic itself is right: 2500 x 5400 = 13 500 000 J and 13 500 000 / 230 = 58 696 C. Replaced with a plain comma.
findings.evidence: recomputation; KaTeX auto-render only processes delimited spans

findings.claim: '... state the units at every step - examiners award marks for clear working.'
findings.truth: An invented claim about examiner behaviour. Reworded to describe the benefit of clear working without asserting how marks are given.
findings.evidence: house rule on invented exam claims

findings.claim: 'This produces an alternating current (a.c.) - the voltage reverses direction once per revolution of the magnet.'
findings.truth: The induced p.d. reverses every half turn, so it reverses twice per revolution and one revolution gives one complete cycle. The lesson contradicted itself: flashcard 6 and the mark scheme for practice question 4 both say the direction reverses each half-turn.
findings.evidence: settled fact for a simple alternator; spec P3.7.4 requires explaining the p.d./time graph of an alternator

findings.claim: 'the two sides of the coil that are parallel to the field axis experience opposite forces'
findings.truth: A conductor lying parallel to the field feels no force at all, as the same lesson states two paragraphs earlier. The sides that produce the turning effect are the ones at right angles to the field. Reworded.
findings.evidence: spec P3.6 narrative 'If the current-carrying wire is placed at right angles to the magnetic field lines, the force will be at right angles to both'; F = BIl sin(theta)

findings.claim: The content_html higher-only wrappers in this lesson are correct, but the same Higher-only material is untagged in the two motor/generator takeaways, the whole exam tip, three knowledge checks, eight flashcards and four practice questions.
findings.truth: Every assessable outcome in P3.6 (motor effect, Fleming's left-hand rule, F = BIl, the electric motor) and every one in P3.7 (induction, alternator, dynamo, transformers, both transformer equations) is bold, so all of it is Higher tier only, and P3.7 is separate science only as well. Takeaways and the exam tip take a '(Higher tier)' prefix, knowledge checks a '(Higher tier)' prefix on the question, flashcards a '(Higher tier)' tag at the end of the question, practice questions an '(HT)' suffix on the type. The one bullet that already carried '(Higher Tier)' put it after F = BIl only, implying the motor effect and Fleming's rule were both-tier; the tag moves to the front. Knowledge check 4 and flashcards 7 and 8 are left alone: solenoids, electromagnets and induced magnets are P3.5, both tiers, and a transformer's job in the National Grid is P2.2.5.
findings.evidence: -bold file: P3.6.1-P3.6.4 and P3.7.1-P3.7.8 all bold; P3.5.1-P3.5.8 not bold

findings.claim: Flashcard 9 answer: 'Any two: MRI scanners, scrapyard cranes, electric motors, loudspeakers, circuit breakers.'
findings.truth: A five-item comma list, which the house flashcard rule does not allow. Rewritten as one sentence naming two examples, both drawn from the P3.5 Ideas about Science column.
findings.evidence: house flashcard rule: no list answers

findings.claim: The sections 'The Three-Pin Plug' (wire colours) and 'Fuses and Circuit Breakers' carry a heading, a key fact, a worked example, two knowledge checks, a matching knowledge check, three flashcards and a 6-mark practice question.
findings.truth: J259 has no fuse, circuit-breaker or wire-colour statement anywhere. P2.2.6 asks only for the functions of the live, neutral and earth wires, the potential differences between them, why a live wire is dangerous with the switch open, and the danger of connecting live to an earthed object - all of which the lesson does cover correctly. The fuse and colour material is AQA and Edexcel content used here as context. Not deleted: it is correct physics and useful, and removing it would ripple through narration, four knowledge checks and three flashcards. Flagged so a later pass can decide whether to label it as background or rebalance the 6-mark question onto an on-spec outcome. The lesson also never states the actual potential differences between the three wires, which P2.2.6 does require.
findings.evidence: grep of specs/ocr/physics-b-21c-J259.md for 'fuse' and 'circuit breaker': no hits in P2 or P3

findings.claim: The section 'Uses and Hazards of Static Electricity' teaches electrostatic paint sprayers, laser printers and photocopiers, fuel-tanker earthing and anti-static wristbands.
findings.truth: P3.1 asks only for the production of static and sparking by rubbing, the electron-transfer explanation, and the electric-field explanation. These applications are AQA and Edexcel content. They are correct physics and reasonable unfamiliar contexts, so they are labelled here rather than removed. No exam claim is attached to them.

findings.claim: Flashcards 4 and 7 ask learners to give F = BIl and the transformer turns ratio from memory.
findings.truth: Section 5h puts F = BIl (P3.6.3), Vp Ip = Vs Is (P3.4.5 / P3.7.8a) and Vp/Vs = Np/Ns (P3.7.8b) in list (b), 'select from a list and apply' - they are given in the exam, not recalled. Nothing in the lesson claims they must be recalled, so no edit; recorded so the wording is not tightened into a false recall claim later. The recall equations this unit does use (E = Pt, efficiency, Q = It, V = IR, V = W/Q, P = E/t, E = QV, P = VI, P = I squared R) are all in list (a) and none of them is bold.
findings.evidence: spec 5h Equations in Physics, lists (a) and (b)

findings.truth: The unit maps to chapter P2 (Sustainable energy) and chapter P3 (Electric circuits): L1 = P2.1 + P2.2 + P3.4.6; L2 = P3.1 (separate science only); L3 = P3.2 + P3.3; L4 = P3.4 plus P2.2.4 and P2.2.6; L5 = P3.5 + P3.6 + P3.7 (P3.7 separate science only). Untaught outcomes in the mapped chapters: P3.2.2 (charge = current x time is never stated as an equation, only used inside an L4 worked example); P3.2.7 (circuit symbols and the positive/negative terminal convention); P3.3.1 (potential difference = work done / charge is described in words in L3 but the equation is never given); P3.3.5b (light intensity on an LDR in a sensing circuit) and the potential-divider practical work; P3.7.2 (the moving coil microphone); P3.7.5 (adapting an alternator into a dynamo with a split-ring commutator, and its p.d./time graph). No paper-split claim appears anywhere in the unit, which is correct: both the Breadth and the Depth paper assess all chapters at each tier.
findings.evidence: spec 2a specification overview; P3.2, P3.3, P3.7 outcome lists

summary: Two HIGH factual errors (mains a.c. reverses 100 times a second not 50; an alternator's p.d. reverses every half turn not once per revolution) plus a motor-coil orientation error. The Higher-tier wrapper is wrong in both directions: both-tier efficiency (L1) and both-tier transformer/National Grid content (L4) were hidden from Foundation readers, while the correctly wrapped Higher-only P3.6 and P3.7 material in L5 leaked untagged into takeaways, the exam tip, three knowledge checks, eight flashcards and four practice questions. Seven practice questions carried an (HT) tag on both-tier content and one used AQA 'required practical' wording. Every calculation in the unit recomputes correctly and every knowledge-check answer key is right.
